intelligence.human_view: The corner jewels were the small thing that gave the page away: not clear, not sharp, not reading as an object — so the corners read as decoration instead of as a seal. The original emblem is the fix because it is already the thing: a crowned jewel with wings, drawn once, properly. Taking it verbatim — never redrawing it — is the harvest-first law applied to the house's own mark: the emblem is not a design problem to solve, it is an object to place. On an angle in each corner it gives the high-level effect — the page reads official because the seal on it is real. And it belongs on certificates and documents for the same reason: the official areas carry the official mark, always the same, always clear.
intelligence.simple_view: The little jewels in the corners aren't clear enough! Here's the real one — the pretty purple diamond with the crown and wings. Put the real one in every corner, tilted on an angle, and it looks so fancy and official!
